category_title: At-risk students in Applied courses with learned helplessness and inconsistent engagement
minimal_context: The student's small group is called to the front of the classroom to share their project with the whole class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for your group to come up to the front and share your project with the whole class.

STUDENT: I don't want to go up there. I don't like being wrong in front of everyone.

TUTOR: Everyone needs to present. Just go up and show us what order you put things in.

STUDENT: Fine. But I know it's wrong. I'm stupid and I'm always going to fail anyway.

TUTOR: Just start explaining your project to the class.

STUDENT: No, I'm not doing it! The other kids love pointing out mistakes and are just going to say 'well no, you can't put that there because...' and make fun of me.

options.A: Ensure that the group's project is accurate and meets the activity objectives before having them present.
options.B: Interrupt the student and explicitly ask the rest of the class whether they agree with the group's project.
options.C: Provide help to the student in the form of giving explicit instructions for solving peer conflicts.
options.D: Establish 'hands down and think' time during the presentation, after which any student may be asked to contribute.
